Program Definition nat_compose `{F : C ⟶ D} {G : C ⟶ D} {K : C ⟶ D} (f : G ⟹ K) (g : F ⟹ G) : F ⟹ K := {| transform := λ X, transform[f] X ∘ transform[g] X |}.

Class Transform := { transform {x} : F x ~> G x; naturality {x y} (f : x ~> y) : fmap[G] f ∘ transform ≈ transform ∘ fmap[F] f; naturality_sym {x y} (f : x ~> y) : transform ∘ fmap[F] f ≈ fmap[G] f ∘ transform }.

statement_record.book: For a locally small C, the set-valued functors P, Q : C ⟶ Sets (diagrams on C; contravariantly, presheaves on C) and the natural transformations between them form a category Sets^C, with identities and composition computed componentwise, so that a commuting triangle of natural transformations evaluates at every object to a commuting triangle of functions, with a naturality cylinder over it for each arrow f : D → C.
statement_record.intree: Program Definition Fun : Category := {| obj := C ⟶ D; hom := @Transform C D; id := @nat_id C D; compose := @nat_compose C D |}, where nat_compose has transform := λ X, transform[f] X ∘ transform[g] X and Transform carries the naturality square fmap[G] f ∘ transform ≈ transform ∘ fmap[F] f.
statement_record.strength_comparison: same (in-tree stronger by generality): the library builds [C, D] for an ARBITRARY codomain D, of which Sets^C = [C, Sets] and Sets^(C^op) = [C^op, Sets] are instances (Theory/Sheaf.v:127/133 name the latter Presheaves/Copresheaves). statement_record.book: Definition 8.1. The Yoneda embedding is the functor y : C ⟶ Sets^(C^op) sending each object C to the contravariant representable presheaf yC = Hom_C(−, C) : C^op ⟶ Sets, and each arrow f : C → D to the natural transformation yf = Hom_C(−, f) : Hom(−, C) → Hom(−, D), i.e. componentwise postcomposition with f.

Presentational differences only: hom-collections are setoids and each component is a SetoidMorphism (respects ≈), and Sets is the category of setoids rather than of sets. statement_record.book: A group G embeds by an injective homomorphism into Aut(|G|) ⊆ |G|^|G| by g ↦ left translation, with (g·h)~ = g~ ∘ h~; likewise any monoid M into End(|M|). This representation is faithful but NOT full — there are self-maps of |G| that are not left translations. Fullness is recovered by restricting to RIGHT-EQUIVARIANT maps: if α(x·g) = α(x)·g for all g then α is itself a left translation. This is the prototype of the extra structure the Yoneda embedding puts on objects.

Nearest in-tree fact, deliberately NOT counted as partial coverage: Theory/Functor.v:355 FullyFaithful `(F : C ⟶ D) `{@Full _ _ F} `{@Faithful _ _ F} : ∀ x y, F x ≅ F y → x ≅ y, which at F = y gives yA ≅ yB → A ≅ B. verifier.notes: My blind search found no counterpart. Independently re-ran the key greps: `rg 'Injective'` — 0 hits tree-wide; no statement of the form fobj[y] A = fobj[y] B → A = B anywhere; no Embedding class to package it into (same finding as awodey:8.2:def-embedding). I read Functor/Hom.v and Functor/Hom/Yoneda.v end to end and confirm nothing of the kind appears. I specifically endorse the log's refusal to count Theory/Functor.v:355 FullyFaithful as partial coverage: yA ≅ yB → A ≅ B is reflection of isomorphisms, a different claim, and is already the content of awodey:8.3:thm3. Note for issue drafting (not a reason to reclassify): the statement IS expressible here — obj is a Type with Coq equality available — but the library systematically avoids object-level equality, and the book's own printed argument for this claim is flagged in the inventory as a draft slip (variables switch from A,B to C,D mid-sentence), so ABSENT should be filed with low priority if at all.
